biography.plain_text: Paulin Richier was a French industrialist who built a construction-equipment manufacturer from a small workshop in Charleville. His company expanded from concrete mixers into road-building machinery and tower cranes, becoming a major European producer with international sales. Ford acquired control in 1972, after rapid expansion had strained the business's finances and management.

long_biography.plain_text:
Machinery manufacturer Paulin Richier filed around fifteen patents on concrete mixers between 1929 and 1939. They addressed practical problems: measuring liquids, mixing materials efficiently and automating the loading and unloading of a machine. His technical background included work as an engineer at Millar's before he established his own company.

Richier also treated service after a sale as part of the manufacturer's job. He wanted customers to know that help would be available on their building sites when equipment needed attention. Alongside that emphasis on support, the company promoted its products through exhibitions, illustrated catalogues and scale models.
